root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: elevation or highness, and return or reversion.
root_idea.development: The elevation branch extends to high ground, increase, yield, surplus, and the first or prime part of something; the separate return branch yields reversion and reply-related uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single Quran-attested nominal is presented under the normalized citation form رِيعٌ.

senses.definition: A high or elevated place or stretch of ground, visible from afar.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ, referring to elevated places on which structures or monuments are built.
An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic expression بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ; the word may be understood as a route or opening through mountainous ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To increase, grow, become abundant, or thrive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of wheat, food, trees and their produce, crops, and camels in the sense that they increase or have many young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become redundant or remain over and above what is required.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of food, flour, or anything left in excess, including something remaining in a person's possession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return, revert, or come back to a former place or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people, camels, vomit, or anything returning; it may also describe returning inward or returning in response to exhortation or a sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw or gather oneself together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural usage describing people collecting or drawing themselves together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become torn or rent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a poetic description in which one side becomes torn when another side is sewn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return a reply or answer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction in which a response is returned to another person; distinct from physical return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ascend or climb upon a high place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with رِيعَةٌ, a noun for an elevated place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To increase or become increased in growth or yield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of wheat and seed-produce that increase or thrive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To increase or augment something, or cause it to grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use applied to a thing that is made to increase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flow, run, or move hither and thither without a direct course; to overflow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of grease, gravy, oil, clarified butter, or water; figuratively, hands may overflow with successive acts of generosity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mirage, to quiver, vibrate, or move to and fro.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the coming and going or agitated motion of a mirage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confounded or perplexed, as though wavering and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use associated with vacillation or loss of direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pause, hesitate, hold back, refrain, or abstain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of delaying or refraining from an affair; the same branch includes holding back from undertaking something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Increase, growth, abundance, or yield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the increase produced by food, land, or other things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Revenue or yield arising from the increase of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived economic use referring to returns from productive land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundant milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in describing a she-camel whose milk is plentiful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surplus, redundancy, residue, or portion left over.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of excess flour or meal, risen dough, seed for sowing, and redundant portions of clothing or armor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first, prime, or most excellent part or period of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the prime of youth or youthful vigor, the early part of the day after sunrise, and the initial or most prominent phase of a phenomenon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A successive pace or rate of movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a she-camel whose pace follows one rate after another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reply or answer, especially in the expression of having none to give.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom فُلَانٌ لَيْسَ لَهُ رَيْعٌ means that a person has no reply or answer to offer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fright or fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use equated with رَوْعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain or elevated mountain mass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader geographical use distinct from the Quranic high-place interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The channel of a valley torrent descending from elevated ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the watercourse formed around or below high land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high mound, heap of sand, or hill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical use for a raised heap or hill, including a raised mound around a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Christian cloister or cell.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized architectural use, synonymous with صَوْمَعَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pigeon-turret or pigeon tower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized architectural use for a structure housing pigeons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gathered company or number of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term applies specifically to men who have drawn or collected themselves together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel abounding in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet for a camel with plentiful milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleet, swift, and excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested as an epithet of a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A register recording the increase or revenue of districts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical administrative term referring to land revenue records.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fertile, fruitful, or abundant in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of land that has much growth or yield.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that goes away to pasture and returns by herself, or is repeatedly ridden back and forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes recurrent departure and return or repeated journeys.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that quickly yields abundant milk or quickly becomes fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized use describing rapid productive increase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slippery or oily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a man who anoints himself with oils.
